text.title: AI selloff deepens as Anthropic slips after debut; Nasdaq futures lead U.S. futures lower
text.summary: U.S. futures point lower after a sixth straight S&P 500 loss. Nasdaq 100 futures are down 1.9%, S&P 500 futures 1.0%, Dow futures 0.3% and Russell 2000 futures 0.4%. Overseas markets sold off hard: Japan fell 5.1% and Hong Kong 3.8%. Treasury yields edged lower and the VIX rose to 30.83, but gold fell 2.9% and oil slipped, so no classic haven is working. The common thread is doubt about the AI trade, which is now spilling into software, commodities and global equities.
text.rates: The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.05%, down 2bp, its fourth straight decline, and the 2-year is 4.76%, down 4bp. That is a modest bid for bonds, but yields remain high enough to pressure equity valuations, especially growth stocks. The dollar index is down 0.2% at 103.64, so there is no dollar-driven flight to safety. Oil and gold are both lower, which signals growth concerns and forced selling more than inflation fears. Bitcoin is down 0.7% at about 61,478.
text.breadth: Asia took the brunt: the Nikkei fell 5.1% and the Hang Seng 3.8%. Europe is also weak, with the Euro Stoxx 50 down 2.3% and the DAX down 2.2%, while the FTSE 100 is down a milder 0.9%. Reuters links Asia's slide to AI jitters, and WSJ says stocks fell across the globe. Bloomberg says global stocks hit their longest losing streak in more than three years. This suggests a rough open in the U.S., led by tech, with small caps and the Dow holding up somewhat better in futures.
text.context: The S&P 500 has fallen six straight sessions, down 5.5% over five days and 7.0% over one month, and sits 7.5% below its one-month high. The Nasdaq is 10.6% below its high. MarketWatch says all four major U.S. indexes are on pace for their worst week since the April 2025 tariff shock. J.P. Morgan's weekly recap, as of Nov 13, noted the S&P 500 at 18.2x forward earnings and pointed to power costs as a pressure point for the AI buildout.
text.takeaway: Sharp, narrative-driven drawdowns like this test diversification, and falling stocks with a weaker gold price is a reminder that no single asset hedges every kind of stress. For long-term investors, the usual lesson is that sentiment can swing quickly while time horizon and portfolio structure stay the anchors.
text.talk: Markets are under pressure globally as doubts about AI spending and returns spread from tech into software and commodities. Volatility is elevated, so it's a good moment to revisit your plan rather than react to a single day's headlines.

drivers.t: Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in total after underwriters took up the overallotment option. Its shares are lower in premarket trading a day after the debut. The FT says the blockbuster listing failed to ease worries about historic AI capital spending. Reuters calls the stumble a reality check for the AI trade. Investors had treated the IPO as a test of appetite for AI risk, and the slide suggests even a record deal can't offset worries about returns on AI spending. That weighs most on richly valued, long-duration tech, which is why Nasdaq futures lag.
drivers.impact: AI sentiment sours, Nasdaq futures lead lower

drivers.t: Bloomberg describes few winners and a sea of losers after Jensen Huang's ouster from Nvidia. CNBC says Anthropic had to list through a crisis at Nvidia. Chip stocks are declining alongside Nasdaq futures. Nvidia sits at the center of AI hardware spending, so leadership uncertainty feeds doubts about the whole supply chain. Democrats have also opened a probe into Nvidia's influence on a U.S. investigation.

Intuit beat on EPS but missed on revenue, and its downbeat outlook is giving investors a fresh reason to worry about legacy software companies. The stock is down 8.0% premarket. A weak forecast matters more than the quarter because it resets expectations for future earnings. The reaction fits the broader fear that AI is disrupting established software models.

WSJ reports AI stocks tumbling across the globe, and Reuters says Asian stocks had their worst week since 2020. Bloomberg notes metals are slumping as traders worry demand will dry up. Gold is down 2.9% to 3579.2, extending a 7.9% five-day decline, and Bloomberg says the rout is testing its all-weather safe-haven reputation. WTI is down 0.6% at 81.99 and 7.4% lower over five days. WSJ attributes the pullback to improving supply and continued Middle East shipping risks. Falling commodities alongside equities point to growth worries, not just an AI-specific story.

Bloomberg says the way the rout is spreading beyond tech echoes patterns before the dotcom crash. Citi's strategists see no compelling reason yet to add risk, and say a key stock-market signal is close to flashing red. A Bank of America strategist warns Wall Street is underpricing hard-landing risk. Such commentary can reinforce selling by encouraging risk reduction, and it helps explain the VIX at a one-month high.

earnings.t: The EPS beat was overshadowed by a revenue miss and a downbeat outlook, which MarketWatch says is adding to Wall Street's worries about legacy software.

watch.why: Citi says a key signal is close to flashing red, which could reinforce risk aversion if it triggers.
